correctness.rationale: Type B root subconfigurations have quotient exponent at most 2, a classical half-integrality phenomenon for bidirected incidence matrices; the self-contained proof here is compatible with that literature. Each genuinely two-sided join then increases the quotient annihilator exponent by at most one, and the dimension recurrence plus barycentric decomposition gives exponent floor((d-1)/2).

originality.rationale: Vallée proves only existence of a uniform exponent via maximal simplex volume. The elementary half-integrality ingredient is classical (Bolker–Zaslavsky 2006), but targeted searches found no explicit floor((d-1)/2) dyadic-decomposition bound or recursive quotient-exponent refinement for type B generalized permutohedra.

value.rationale: The result converts a finiteness-based saturation statement into an explicit intrinsic-dimension bound and determines the optimal universal exponent in dimensions three and four.
